learning_objective: 🌻 Discover the external structures of plants—from the deep roots to the colorful flowers and delicious fruits!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Roots anchor the plant and absorb water. They can be taproots (dicots) or fibrous (monocots). Roots are often modified for storage (carrot, sweet potato) or support (prop roots of banyan). Stems bear leaves and can also be modified for storage (potato, ginger) or protection (thorns).

The main photosynthetic organ. Venation is the arrangement of veins (reticulate in dicots, parallel in monocots). Leaves can be simple (one blade) or compound (divided into leaflets). They can modify into tendrils for climbing (peas) or spines for defense (cactus).

The arrangement of flowers. Racemose: the main axis continues to grow, and flowers are borne laterally in acropetal succession (youngest at top). Cymose: the main axis terminates in a flower (limited growth), flowers in basipetal order.

A typical flower has four whorls: Calyx (sepals, green), Corolla (petals, colorful), Androecium (stamens, male part producing pollen), and Gynoecium (pistil/carpel, female part with ovary, style, and stigma).

The fruit is a ripened ovary developed after fertilization. If a fruit develops without fertilization, it's called parthenocarpic (seedless). The seed is the ripened ovule, containing a seed coat and an embryo (with one or two cotyledons).

fun_activity.title: 🥔 Potato is NOT a Root!
fun_activity.instructions: Go to your kitchen and look closely at a potato. See those little 'eyes' on it? Those are actually axillary buds! Even though potatoes grow underground, they are scientifically modified stems (tubers) meant for storing food, not roots. Sweet potatoes, however, are modified roots!

exam_tips: 📌 Distinguish between reticulate venation (web-like, common in dicots) and parallel venation (straight lines, common in monocots like grass).
📌 Memorize the four types of aestivation (arrangement of petals/sepals): Valvate, Twisted, Imbricate, and Vexillary.
📌 A flower with both male (androecium) and female (gynoecium) reproductive organs is called bisexual.
quick_recap: ⭐ The arrangement of ovules within the ovary is known as placentation (e.g., marginal in peas, parietal in mustard).
⭐ The region of the stem where leaves are born is called a node, and the portion between two nodes is the internode.
⭐ Epigynous flowers have inferior ovaries (e.g., guava, cucumber), while hypogynous flowers have superior ovaries (e.g., mustard).
